title: Reissue, Revocation and Cancellation of Construction Permits 2026
desc: Lost or torn construction permit? How to get it reissued, when a permit is revoked or cancelled, and the documents and deadlines under Decree 217/2026/ND-CP.
summary: A guide to applying for reissue of a lost or torn construction permit and the cases in which a permit is revoked or cancelled under Decree 217/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

The construction permit is a document the homeowner must keep throughout construction and when completing and registering the house in the red book. This article summarises how to apply for reissue when a permit is lost or damaged and the cases in which a permit is revoked or cancelled under Decree 217/2026/ND-CP (effective 1 July 2026).
h2
1. When is a construction permit reissued?
p

Under Article 64 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, a permit is reissued when it is torn, worn out or lost. The reissued permit is a copy of the permit already issued, so its content does not change. To change the design, area, number of floors and so on, an adjustment procedure must be followed – see Adjusting and Extending Construction Permits 2026.
h2
2. Application documents for reissue
ol
An application for reissue of the construction permit in Form No. 02 of Appendix II of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, stating the reason for reissue.
The original or a certified copy of the issued permit – applicable where the permit is torn or worn out. Where it is lost, only the application is needed.
h2
3. Where to submit and how long it takes
ul
The authority that issued the permit is the one that reissues it (Point a, Clause 4, Article 53); for a detached house of a household or individual, this is the commune-level People's Committee.

Submit online through the National Public Service Portal; only when there is a technical problem is a paper submission made at the One-Stop Department or via public postal service (Clause 1, Article 54).
Reissue deadline: 5 working days. If the dossier is incomplete, notice is given once; the homeowner has 1 working day to supplement it (Clauses 1 and 3, Article 54).
Receive the result online or by post and pay the fee as prescribed (Clause 4, Article 54).
h2
4. When is a permit revoked?
p
Under Clause 1, Article 65, a construction permit is revoked when:
ul
The permit was issued contrary to legal regulations;
The project owner fails to remedy building not in accordance with the permit within the period stated in the competent authority's violation-handling document.
p

The authority that issued the permit is competent to revoke it; if that authority does not revoke a wrongly issued permit, the Chairman of the provincial People's Committee decides on revocation directly (Point b, Clause 4, Article 53). For fines for building contrary to the permit, see Fines for Building Without a Permit or Contrary to a Permit.
h2
5. Procedure for revoking and cancelling a permit
ol
Within 10 working days of an inspection conclusion or inspection document determining that the permit falls within the revocation cases, the competent authority issues a revocation decision.
The decision is sent to the project owner, posted on the authority's website and made public at the commune-level People's Committee within 5 working days.
A paper permit must be returned in original within 5 working days of receipt of the revocation decision.

If it is not returned within 10 working days of the revocation decision, the competent authority issues a decision to cancel the permit and announces it on the website of the Department of Construction.
p
After the permit has been returned or cancelled and the obligations required have been completed, the project owner may apply for a new permit (Clauses 3 and 4, Article 65).
h2
6. Notes on keeping the permit
ul

The homeowner must post the content of the permit publicly at the construction site throughout construction (Clause 2, Article 66); failing to do so, a detached house is fined VND 5–10 million (organisation rate; individuals pay half) under Clause 2, Article 25 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP.
Photograph and keep electronic copies of the permit and the stamped drawings to make reissue and as-built completion easier.
note
This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The fee for reissuing a permit is set locally; ask the ward or commune People's Committee that issued the permit.
